title: Lida Ajer cave (Sumatra)
summary: Lida Ajer is a limestone cave in the Padang Highlands of western Sumatra, dug by Eugène Dubois from 1888. Two human teeth from it were shown in 2017 to be Homo sapiens and dated to about 73,000 to 63,000 years ago, among the earliest evidence of modern humans in a rainforest.

uncertainty.note: 73-63 ka is the Westaway et al. (2017) estimate; a later study dates deposition to 68 +/- 5 ka in Marine Isotope Stage 4 (76-59 ka). Dating remains debated.

where.modern_name: Lida Ajer cave, Padang Highlands near Payakumbuh, West Sumatra, Indonesia
where.historical_name: Karst cave in tropical rainforest on Sundaland, Late Pleistocene; no polities exist at this date

importance.justification: Possible earliest evidence of Homo sapiens in tropical rainforest and in Island Southeast Asia.
